piece.caption:
How contractors and small business owners can use AI presentation tools to convert raw project scope into clean client proposals in minutes.

Instead of spending hours adjusting slide layouts in PowerPoint, dedicated tools like Gamma stream styled slide decks automatically based on your scope notes. If you already use chatbots, ChatGPT can generate downloadable .pptx presentation files directly from your prompts. Claude takes it further by creating custom speaker notes for every slide.

Keep in mind that Gamma's free plan AI credits do not refill monthly, so use them selectively for key client pitches. For basic designs, Canva offers a free plan without built-in AI features.

Comment PRESENTATION for the detailed step-by-step tool guide.

Here is the breakdown of top AI presentation tools for client proposals:

1. Gamma: Streams styled slides from raw text prompts. Note: AI credits do not refill monthly on the free plan.
2. ChatGPT: Converts project scope prompts directly into a downloadable .pptx file.
3. Claude: Generates slide content plus speaker notes for each slide, editable on canvas.
4. Canva: All-in-one design platform; free plan available without AI features (paid plans from $12/month).

We independently review every app we recommend in our best apps lists. When you click some of the links on this page, we may earn a commission. Learn more .
The days of spending hours dragging images to just the right place on a slide are far behind us. You can now create a presentation with AI, giving the robots the job of setting the structure, adding the initial content, and executing on the aesthetics of your deck. All you have to do is tweak it with your information, human insights, and flair—and rehearse it a bit before the big performance.
I spent a month testing all the best presentation software, focusing on the ones that use AI in a way that will help you get the presentation you want faster. Based on all my testing, these are the best AI presentation apps.
Canva for an all-in-one presentation and design platform
Beautiful.ai for updating stats over time
Chronicle for clean design and widget-based editing
Prezi for non-linear, zoomable presentations
What makes the best AI presentation-making software?
Our best apps roundups are written by humans who've spent much of their careers using, testing, and writing about software. Unless explicitly stated, we spend dozens of hours researching and testing apps, using each app as it's intended to be used and evaluating it against the criteria we set for the category. We're never paid for placement in our articles from any app or for links to any site—we value the trust readers put in us to offer authentic evaluations of the categories and apps we review. For more details on our process, read the full rundown of how we select apps to feature on the Zapier blog .
Traditional presentation apps offer tools to create as many slides as you need, letting you combine text, images, and animations to support your monthly stats report or pitch deck. Over time, these platforms launched templates with fixed content that you can replace, a starting point to help you save time.
But with AI in the mix, you can get personalized content that better matches your objective. This can both save time and open up new angles, showing you topics you could talk about to make it more thorough and engaging. The best AI presentation makers should have a good balance between providing a viable (and somewhat accurate) first draft and tools to quickly help you edit, refine, and polish.
Here's what I looked for to find the best presentation maker:
AI content generation. Be it text or images, the content needs to make sense when considering your prompt or instructions.
Speed. The point of these apps is to save time, not add complexity. I measured how quick and easy it was to get from the dashboard to a presentation I could edit.
Customization. Ideally, a full kit of customization tools, but I also looked for user experiences with fewer, more direct settings to edit the most important parts.
Exporting and integrations. Just in case you need to present it somewhere else, send it via email, or collaborate with your team.
Pricing. Unless developing presentations is your entire job description, you shouldn't be paying a lot for this speed boost.
I spent a fun month signing up for the 40+ apps on my list, checking out their AI abilities and prompting my way to dozens of presentations on random topics. In the end, I was able to narrow it down to my six top picks.
What about Microsoft Copilot for PowerPoint and Google Gemini for Google Slides?
Microsoft PowerPoint and Google Slides have AI features, the former through Copilot and the latter via Gemini . They were part of this list in the past, but the competition is now fierce: new AI presentation builders offer high output quality and a smooth user experience that neither tech giant has been able to fully achieve yet.
I decided to remove both from the list to make space for new options and to save you some time when making a choice. That being said, if you have a Microsoft or Google subscription, be sure to check out their AI feature sets: they might fit your needs if you're an extremely casual user.
Both OpenAI and Anthropic have been rolling out their tools for building presentations in their chatbot apps. If you already subscribe to either ChatGPT or Claude, start a new chat and ask for a presentation to see if the output matches your needs.
ChatGPT takes your prompt and puts together a presentation in the .pptx file format, generating the text and slides based on your instructions and attached context. You can keep editing by sending more messages to the agent. When you're ready to present, hit the play button at the top-right, and the app goes into full screen.
Claude is a few steps ahead. It does everything that ChatGPT currently does, but also generates speaker notes for each slide. You can add elements or edit text manually in the canvas for minor changes, and insert new slides with a predetermined layout, ready to fill.
The major advantage of using either option is that you can leverage your existing integrations. When you connect your knowledge from Google Drive or Notion, you can put the agent to work on your data, not on general training or web searches.
Having said all that, neither made the cut for this list because their feature sets are limited compared with dedicated AI presentation makers.
The best AI presentation makers at a glance
Advanced customization settings for visual harmony
An all-in-one presentation and design platform
Strong branding and collaboration features
Free plan available without AI features; from $12/month

If your team's presentations are missing that special spark, it's time to upgrade: Gamma builds beautiful presentations that make design experts jealous, helping you make all your presentations more engaging without extra effort. And, since it also covers documents, social media carousels, websites, and image generation, it offers a lot of value in a single subscription.
Currently in version 5, the Gamma engine offers more visual variety when compared with previous versions, delivering more creative results, especially if you prompt it to impress. But even with a basic prompt, it builds a theme that matches the topic, balancing text-only slides with image slides to make presentations more engaging.
When generating with AI, type in the topic of your presentation and choose the number of slides. First, you get an outline of the presentation to see if it covers everything you need: add or reorganize the cards to choose what you'd like. Scrolling down, the extra knobs let you adjust how much text should be in each slide, determine the image source (automatic, web images, or AI), and add a prompt for the image style.
